items.prompt:
Edit the HAIR PAINTING ONLY in image 1 to match the hair painting of the curse series in images 2 and 3.
REFERENCE ROLES: Image 1 is the edit target; preserve its current half-body composition, face and violet eyes, head angle, expression, crescent ornament location, black priestess clothing, cape, two gloved hands, purple shadow claw and gray background. Images 2 (curse-drain) and 3 (curse-silence) are the SPECIFIC HAIR-PAINTING references. Match their actual paint grammar and hair colors, without copying their pose, face direction, red spell elements or backgrounds.

The target hair currently has soft rounded ribbon-like locks and a braid that looks smoothly sculpted. Rebuild it in the curse references' opaque, deliberate broad paint planes: cool pale ivory/light muted golden base, broad blue-gray shadow planes and occasional warm stone-gray underside planes. Use a small number of flatter elongated paint strokes with hard handmade turns and irregular broken ends, as in references 2 and 3. Highlights are contiguous pale planes selectively interrupted by the underlying gray paint, not glossy ribbons, smooth rounded gradients or numerous pale scratches. Quiet base-color areas remain large.
Preserve the current hairstyle silhouette: rounded crown, dense straight fringe, two long straight cheek sidelocks and one low thick side braid at image-left. Paint the crown as a few coherent broad directional planes like reference 3; the fringe groups are substantial with a few selected dark boundary accents like reference 2. Sidelocks have broad quiet pale planes and occasional narrow but purposeful edge turns, not fine strand networks. Paint each braid segment as a large interlocking block with a clear muted gray underside and broad pale top plane, reflecting the braid in reference 3; simplify the taper into a few connected shapes. Keep selective angular handmade brush transitions, but do not fragment it into micro facets or mosaic.
Hair visible color should directly follow the references' pale ivory, muted blue-gray and warm-gray relationships. The target is not bright white plastic hair, yellow/gold hair, silver chrome or uniform gray. Reduce softness and overmodeling while retaining volume through a few broad plane changes. Faces and eyes stay the clearest selective detail; hair remains coarse and quiet. No all-over texture, fine hair strokes, scratch marks, dense chipped highlights, glossy 3D, airbrush or vector-flat fill. Keep all non-hair content close to image 1. No text, watermark, frame or UI.
